children: Crude oil futures are surging more than 4% on Thursday following a tanker attack in the Persian Gulf and the shutdown of some production in the U.S. Gulf as the region braces for a hurricane.

A tanker was struck by projectiles off the coast of Qatar, according to the U.K. Maritime Trade Operations Centre, as Iran appears to be intensifying its attacks on shipping after the U.S. had recently succeeded in restoring crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.

"The frequency ​of Iranian attacks on ships ⁠is now at the highest point since the war began and likely to intensify further," MST Marquee head of energy Saul Kavonic said in a note. "Constrained product flows, extreme logistics costs, and high likelihood of Iranian escalation ​are keeping prices elevated."
Elsewhere in the Middle East,
by Yemen's Houthi militants damaged two Saudi airports, escalating a conflict that threatens oil flows through the Red Sea.
Oil prices are also gaining on supply curtailments as Hurricane Isaias moves toward ​offshore production areas ⁠in the U.S. Gulf, causing companies to shut their platforms.
Chevron
said it has begun shut-in procedures at four of its assets in the U.S. Gulf, and Shell
said it has halted production and evacuated personnel at five of its Gulf sites and has moved non-essential personnel from another.
The U.S. Marine Minerals Administration said 511K bbl/day, or 25% of current Gulf production, had been shut in as of midday Wednesday.
Also, the Trump administration reportedly has asked the Pentagon to develop strike options against Iranian targets that could be exercised ahead of the U.S. midterm election.

Concerns over continued attacks on shipping in the Middle East are lifting European natural gas prices, adding to worries about liquefied natural gas supplies, as European Union underground natural gas storage facilities are just 72% full, according to data from industry group Gas Infrastructure Europe, well below the seasonal average.
Dutch TTF natural gas, the European benchmark, traded Thursday at ~
80/MWh, nearly 1.5x higher than just before the start of the Iran war.
Front-month Nymex crude
for November delivery jumped 4.4% to $92.20/bbl, and front-month Brent crude
for December delivery climbed 4.5% to $104.71/bbl.
Five of the day's 10 biggest gainers on the S&P 500 are from the oil and gas sector: APA Corp.
up 3.7%, Marathon Petroleum
up 3.6%, Valero Energy
up 3.1%, Diamondback Energy
up 2.7%, Chevron
